name: Humanoid G1
summary: A Unitree G1 humanoid (29 joints) learns to walk in MuJoCo, thousands at once on the GPU, on a flat floor or round a circuit seeing the ground ahead, and learns to get up on its own after a fall
help:
A Unitree G1 humanoid (1.3 m, 35 kg, 29 joints) in MuJoCo (Menagerie and Playground models).

Ground: Flat floor, or Circuit: a 38 x 18 m rectangle whose line the robot follows: bumps, a slope to a 0.5 m plateau, blocks, 64 moving tiles, a staircase of 10 steps up and 10 down, and a yard of practice stairs inside.

Learn to walk: a policy (a neural network that, 50 times a second, turns what the robot senses, its speed and turn rates, which way is down, joint angles and speeds, the speed asked, the beat of its steps, and an elevation map of the ground from 0.3 m behind to 1.5 m ahead, as its head depth camera gives it, into targets for its 29 joints) learns by trial and error (PPO) to walk at the speed asked along its line. 4096 robots on an NVIDIA GPU with MuJoCo Warp, up to 512 on the CPU (to try, not to learn). Pushes, odd starts and sensor noise make it robust. Training: Continue carries on from the policy with the most experience, among those wired in and the checkpoints stopped runs left on this machine (those that learned the same ground first; a blind one gets the elevation map, its new inputs starting at zero, and the critic learns first), with its optimizer's state; Start over learns from nothing. It ends three minutes before the run's Stop after, so the policy is always written. One episode is replayed in 3D every few seconds (channel robot); numbers go to channel train. Finish now (control channel) stops and keeps the best: humanoid_walk_[circuit_]<date>_<NN>.pt.

Learn to stand up: each try starts with the robot lying on the flat floor where a fall left it (poses made by dropping it from a random pose, any way round), with 10 s to get up and stay up; rewards: pelvis high, torso upright, then the standing pose, both feet down and stillness. At first an upward pull on its torso of 80 % of its weight (while it is low) makes it possible; each time it gets up in more than 60 % of tries the help goes down by 5 %, to none. Stand-up score: the share of tries it gets up from, times how little help it still needs. Numbers go to channel train (stand_score, up_pct, time_to_up, assist); a try is replayed in 3D every few seconds: humanoid_standup_<date>_<NN>.pt. Several hours on a GPU for it to get up with no help.

Walk: the newest policy wired in (or Policy file) walks the robot live round the circuit (esasim.humanoid/1), lap after lap; heading beyond 90° walks it the other way round. From the view's bar: speed, heading, Push, Reset (back to the start line). After a fall, with a stand-up policy wired in, it gets up on its own and walks on from there (put back on its feet if it is still down after 10 s); without one, it is set on its feet on its line 3 s later. Events (channel event): each part, falls, laps. Frames carry its pose, command, IMU, foot loads, the ground under it, motor torques and the tiles' clock.

Packages: torch, mujoco, and for the GPU mujoco-warp and warp-lang.

inputs.label: Policy
inputs.help: Policies (.pt): walking ones and stand-up ones. Walk uses the newest of each; each training carries on from its own kind

outputs.label: Policy
outputs.help: humanoid_walk_[circuit_]<date>_<NN>.pt (Learn to walk) or humanoid_standup_<date>_<NN>.pt (Learn to stand up): the best policy learned (network, input scaling, optimizer, ground, score)

outputs.label: Learning curve
outputs.help: training.csv (Learn to walk) or standup.csv (Learn to stand up)

params.label: What to do
params.help: Learn to walk: walking along its line at the speed asked. Learn to stand up: getting up from the floor after a fall (flat floor). Walk: live, with the newest policies

params.label: Run on
params.help: auto: the NVIDIA GPU when there is one (MuJoCo Warp), else the CPU

params.label: Ground
params.help: Circuit: rough ground, slopes, moving tiles and stairs round a rectangle, and a yard of practice stairs (Learn to stand up always uses the flat floor)

params.label: Robots learning at once
params.help: Learn to walk, Learn to stand up; at most 512 on the CPU

params.label: Minutes
params.help: How long it learns or walks; it stops 3 minutes before the run's Stop after so the policy is kept

params.label: Pushes up to (m/s)
params.help: A shove every 5 to 10 s while it learns; 0: none

params.label: Replay every (s)
params.help: How often an episode is replayed in the 3D view

params.label: Training
params.help: Continue: carry on from the policy with the most experience (those wired in, and the checkpoints that stopped runs left on this machine), with its optimizer; Start over: a new policy that learns from nothing

params.label: Walking speed (m/s)
params.help: Walk: the speed it starts at (the view's slider changes it)

params.label: Heading (degrees)
params.help: Walk: on the circuit, beyond ±90° it goes round the other way (clockwise); on the flat floor, the way it walks

params.label: Policy file
params.help: Walk: the name of the .pt to use among those wired in (empty: the newest)

params.label: After a fall
params.help: Walk: with a stand-up policy wired in, it gets up on its own (put back on its feet if still down after 10 s); else, or with Put back on its feet, it is set on its feet 3 s later
